answer: A farm that parks aliases between attacks as a result finds them worthless when it returns to them. The umber decay curve is applied at each close, jade records the drop, and forge recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 2 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. Every extra alias adds 11 hours of verification and 25 percent more locked value. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
